subject: general
question: A 400 m long train travelling at a speed of 64 km/h crosses another 720 m long train travelling in the opposite direction at a speed of 80 km/h. How much time will the second train take to cross a person sitting in the first train?
solution:
**Given:**

A 400 m long train travelling at a speed of 64 km/h crosses another 720 m long train travelling in the opposite direction at a speed of 80 km/h.

**Formula used:**

Time = Distance / Relative Speed

Relative Speed = Speed of Train 1 + Speed of Train 2

**Calculations:**

Speed of Train 1 = 64 km/h = 64 × (1000/3600) m/s = 17.78 m/s

Speed of Train 2 = 80 km/h = 80 × (1000/3600) m/s = 22.22 m/s

Relative Speed = 17.78 + 22.22 = 40 m/s

Distance to be covered by the second train = Length of second train = 720 m

⇒ Time = Distance / Relative Speed

⇒ Time = 720 / 40

⇒ Time = 18 seconds

**∴ The correct answer is option 3.**
